page: Amazon Web Services r8ib.xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server built on the AWS Nitro System. It operates on 64-bit Intel x86_64 architecture with processors clocked at 3.9 GHz. The virtual instance provides 4 dedicated vCPUs distributed across 2 physical cores, running 2 threads per core. System memory is sized at 32.0 GB, establishing an 8.0 GB per-vCPU ratio suited for workloads requiring substantial RAM relative to compute capacity.

Hardware configurations on r8ib.xlarge do not incorporate local storage disks, necessitating the use of remote volumes such as Amazon Elastic Block Store for operating system installation and persistent data management. Networking performance includes a baseline bandwidth allocation of 4 Gbps. The server operates purely on host CPU resources without dedicated hardware accelerators or GPUs.

By delivering an expansive memory footprint alongside moderate compute density, r8ib.xlarge provides qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound tasks that do not require high core counts. Relying on remote storage introduces external latency considerations compared to local NVMe solutions, making it best matched for in-memory databases, Redis or Memcached instances, enterprise application hosting, and moderate data analytics pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services r8ib.xlarge is a memory-optimized server powered by 3.9 GHz Intel x86_64 processors running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It delivers 4 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped to 2 physical cores and includes 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a high 8.0 GB per-vCPU allocation. The instance does not include bundled local disk storage, relying on external network-attached storage for persistent block volumes, and includes no GPU hardware accelerators. Network capacity is provisioned at a baseline speed of 4 Gbps. The high memory-to-vCPU ratio offers favorable resource efficiency for workloads constrained primarily by memory rather than compute throughput. Consequently, r8ib.xlarge is well structured for in-memory caches, distributed data stores, relational database servers, and memory-intensive business backend applications.
